expectations.text: States the intended reader and what they already know, in frontmatter or the opening
expectations.evidence: No frontmatter and no opening statement of the intended reader or what they know; opening only describes the preview URL and its use.

expectations.text: The first paragraph tells the reader that every PR gets a preview environment and where to find it (the pr-<number>.preview.acme.dev URL)
expectations.evidence: Line 3: 'Every pull request gets its own running copy of the web app at `https://pr-<number>.preview.acme.dev`'.

expectations.text: Does not explain Docker basics such as what an image or a container is
expectations.evidence: Only 'Builds the Docker image from the repository's Dockerfile.' No definition of image or container.

expectations.text: Explains Vault, or the secret/preview/web path, at first use in words a reader new to it can act on
expectations.evidence: Line 35-37 at first use: 'read secrets from **Vault**, our secrets store, under the path `secret/preview/web`... To add a new secret, ask the platform team to add it under `secret/preview/web`.'

expectations.text: Explains mailhog, or what happens to emails in a preview, at first use
expectations.evidence: Line 31 at first use: 'Emails are not sent. They are captured by MailHog, which you can read at https://pr-<number>.preview.acme.dev/mailhog.'

expectations.text: Omits the story of trying ephemeral databases first, or reduces it to a single sentence of rationale
expectations.evidence: No mention of ephemeral databases or seeded fixtures anywhere.

expectations.text: Writes the concurrent-push failure with the condition (two pushes within about a minute) before the instruction (re-run the job)
expectations.evidence: Line 59: symptom, then 'Two pushes landed within about a minute of each other...' then 'Re-run the failed job from the PR's Checks tab.' Condition precedes instruction.

expectations.text: States what the reader cannot do: no ssh, and kubectl exec needs staging access most developers lack
expectations.evidence: Line 49-55: 'There is no SSH. If you have access to the staging cluster, open a shell with: kubectl -n previews exec ... Most developers do not have staging cluster access.'

expectations.text: Every heading names its content specifically, and no heading is directly followed by another heading
expectations.evidence: No heading follows a heading, but several headings are generic labels that do not name specific content: 'Lifecycle', 'Data', 'Secrets', 'Logs', 'Troubleshooting', 'Cost'.
